title: Visigoths
capsule: The Visigoths were a Gothic confederation who, following the Gothic crossing of the Danube in 376 CE, won the Battle of Adrianople in 378 and eventually settled within Roman territories as federates. Under Alaric I they sacked Rome on 24 August 410—a seismic psychological blow to the empire—and subsequently moved into Gaul; by 418 Emperor Honorius granted them the region of Aquitaine as a formal settlement (the Toulouse kingdom), marking the first Germanic kingdom established on Roman soil. The 396–426 window recorded here covers Alaric's Italian campaigns through the consolidation of the Visigothic settlement in Aquitaine under Theodoric I.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Visigothic territorial presence in this period is documented in Roman literary and administrative sources; precise boundaries of federate territory are approximate.
